title: Impact of Restricted Inflow of Foreign Workers on Population and Companies' Operations
what_it_is: Impact of Restricted Inflow of Foreign Workers on Population and Companies' Operations

sections.label: Work Permit holders decline
sections.summary: In 2020, Work Permit holders in the CMP sectors declined by nearly 60,000, about 16%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In 2020, the number of Work Permit holders in the CMP sectors declined by nearly 60,000 or about 16%.

sections.label: Entry approvals monthly average
sections.summary: From November 2020 to April 2021, entry approvals averaged 5,100 S Pass and Work Permit holders per month.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: From November 2020 right up to April 2021, we granted entry approvals to an average of 5,100 S Pass and Work Permit holders per month.

sections.label: Foreign worker levy rebates increase
sections.summary: Foreign worker levy rebates for Work Permit holders in CMP sectors rise from $90 to $250 per month from May to December 2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Because this is the only way we can ensure the safe inflow of the workers, whilst managing and mitigating the risk of transmission in our community.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, to help businesses tap on workers from other countries, the Government recently announced that we are increasing the existing foreign worker levy rebates for Work Permit holders in the CMP sectors from $90 to $250 per Work Permit holder per month.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: This will last from May to December 2021.

sections.label: IPA extension for work pass holders
sections.summary: The passage asks how long MOM proposes to extend the IPA of Work Permit and S Pass holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, how long is MOM proposing to extend the IPA of Work Permit and S Pass holders respectively in view of their repeated unsuccessful entry pass applications?

sections.label: IPA validity, refunds, source diversification
sections.summary: The extension of IPA validity and refunds are under review, and non-traditional source countries are being explored.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Because we have no way of telling how the pandemic, the control of the situation, the number of infections, the successive wave of infections from many of these source countries where we get our workers from, can actually provide certainty of control of the outbreak of these infections.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, to that end itself, I guess the long answer to your question is that the extension of the validity of these IPAs is something that we are now reviewing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: To the second point about refunds and reimbursements, indeed, we are considering that as well.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For the diversification of source countries, across the different Ministries – MND, BCA, ourselves, as well as MOT and ICA – we are exploring that collectively and we have started to reach out to counterparts in many of these other source countries, the non-traditional sources, to see how we can onboard them.

sections.label: Net outflow of workers
sections.summary: From March 2020 to April this year, CMP sectors saw an average net outflow of 2,400 workers a month.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: If I may sort of couch it this way: net net, in the entire industry itself, from March of 2020, right up till April this year, for the CMP sectors, which include the Work Pass as well as the S Pass, there is an average net outflow of 2,400 workers a month.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: If you just take construction alone, the net outflow is about 1,800 per month.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For the services sector, which we sort of follow through, we are about 42,000 lower than last year, same period, that means March 2020.

sections.label: Worker inflow resumption
sections.summary: From November to April, about 5,100 workers per month entered to address severe acute shortage across all industries.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: From November last year till April this year, when we started to resume opening up the inflow of workers to address our severe acute shortage in all of our industries, on the average per month – as I have alluded to in my earlier statement – 5,100 workers came in for that few months.
